title: Food Journey Team
subtitle: How does one bite of food become energy your body can use?
coreQuestion: Where does food go inside the body after we eat it?
learningGoals: Know digestion is a route, not only the stomach working.
Recognize the order: mouth, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine.
Understand food is broken down and absorbed to help the body get energy.
misconceptions: Digestion only happens in the stomach.
Food disappears directly in the belly.
More realistic anatomy always means better science for children.

hero.title: Food Journey Team
hero.lead: Food does not simply disappear; it travels along a route inside the body.
hero.sceneExplanation: The main scene is a gentle icon-like body route: from the mouth, through the esophagus to the stomach, then to the small and large intestines, with nutrients becoming little energy stars.
hero.childPrompt: Start at the mouth and help one bite of food find the next stop.
hero.parentPrompt: Focus on sequence and function, not realistic anatomy.

classificationGroups.name: Entry and preparation
classificationGroups.childExplanation: The mouth and teeth make food smaller.
classificationGroups.parentNote: Chewing is the first step of digestion.

classificationGroups.name: Transport tube
classificationGroups.childExplanation: The esophagus is a soft tube that sends food to the stomach.
classificationGroups.parentNote: Avoid confusing it with the airway.
classificationGroups.misconception: Food just drops into the belly.

classificationGroups.name: Mixing and breaking down
classificationGroups.childExplanation: The stomach keeps mixing food so it becomes softer and smaller.
classificationGroups.parentNote: Use a mixing bag or kitchen metaphor.
classificationGroups.misconception: The stomach does all digestion alone.

classificationGroups.name: Absorb and sort
classificationGroups.childExplanation: The small intestine absorbs nutrients; the large intestine sorts what remains.

representativeObjects.name: Mouth
representativeObjects.childExplanation: The food journey starts in the mouth.
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking the mouth only eats and does not digest.

representativeObjects.name: Teeth
representativeObjects.childExplanation: Teeth break food into smaller pieces.

representativeObjects.name: Saliva
representativeObjects.childExplanation: Saliva makes food wet and soft.
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking saliva has nothing to do with digestion.

representativeObjects.name: Esophagus
representativeObjects.childExplanation: The esophagus carries food from the mouth to the stomach.
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Mixing it up with the airway.

representativeObjects.name: Stomach
representativeObjects.childExplanation: The stomach mixes food and makes it softer and smaller.
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking the stomach absorbs all nutrients.

representativeObjects.name: Small intestine
representativeObjects.childExplanation: The small intestine absorbs many nutrients the body needs.
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking it is not important because it is called small.

representativeObjects.name: Large intestine
representativeObjects.childExplanation: The large intestine sorts what remains and helps keep some water.

representativeObjects.name: Energy
representativeObjects.childExplanation: The body uses nutrients to grow, run, jump, and think.
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking food only fills the belly.

mechanism.title: How does food finish its body journey?

steps.childExplanation: Teeth break food down and saliva makes it wet.
After swallowing, food moves through the esophagus to the stomach.
The stomach is like a moving bag that mixes food.
The small intestine sends useful nutrients to the body.
The large intestine sorts what remains and keeps some water.

secondaryMechanism.title: Why does food give us energy?

steps.childExplanation: Big food becomes small parts the body can handle.
Nutrients are sent to many places in the body.
The body uses them to run, grow, repair, and think.

comparePairs.title: Only stomach vs Whole route
comparePairs.childConclusion: Digestion is a team route, not a stomach-only job.

comparePairs.title: Small intestine vs Large intestine
comparePairs.childConclusion: Their names sound similar, but their jobs are different.

comparePairs.title: Food vs Energy

b.name: Energy
points: cannot be seen but can be felt

comparePairs.childConclusion: Food helps the body get energy.

clickTasks.title: Tap the food journey stations in order
clickTasks.prompt: Start at the mouth and help food travel the whole route.
clickTasks.wrongHint: Start where food enters the body.
clickTasks.successCopy: You helped food complete its body journey!

clickTasks.title: Find: where are many nutrients absorbed?
clickTasks.prompt: Find the station that absorbs many nutrients.
clickTasks.wrongHint: It is called small, but it is long and important.
clickTasks.successCopy: Correct! The small intestine absorbs many nutrients.

clickTasks.title: Who completes digestion?

wrongHints.only-stomach: The stomach matters, but the mouth and intestines also work.
wrongHints.only-mouth: The mouth is the first stop, but many stops follow.

clickTasks.successCopy: Right! Digestion is a route of body parts working together.

speakTemplates: Food first goes to ____, then through ____.
The small intestine helps the body _____.
Digestion is not only ____; it is ____.
parentTips: Keep digestion icon-like and gentle; avoid realistic organ photos.
At meals, say that chewing slowly helps the first station work well.
If the child asks about poop, simply say the body sorts what remains.

intro: After food enters the body, it is like taking a little train ride.
It passes different stations and becomes nutrients and energy the body can use.
keyFacts: Teeth break food into smaller pieces.
The esophagus sends food to the stomach.
The small intestine absorbs many nutrients.
The large intestine sorts what remains.
copy.explainPrompt: Can you name the body stations food visits in order?

acceptanceCriteria: The child can say mouth, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine in order.
The child knows digestion is not only the stomach working.
The child can explain food as becoming smaller, absorbed, and used as energy.

visualEvidenceBindings.observePrompt: Compare visual clues for Only stomach and Whole route.
visualEvidenceBindings.evidenceCopy: Only stomach: one station only; forgets mouth and intestines; incomplete explanation. Whole route: has entrance and later stations; organs cooperate; closer to the real process. Digestion is a team route, not a stomach-only job.

visualEvidenceBindings.observePrompt: Compare visual clues for Small intestine and Large intestine.
visualEvidenceBindings.evidenceCopy: Small intestine: thin and long; absorbs many nutrients; very important. Large intestine: thicker; sorts what remains; helps keep some water. Their names sound similar, but their jobs are different.

visualEvidenceBindings.observePrompt: Compare visual clues for Food and Energy.
visualEvidenceBindings.evidenceCopy: Food: can be seen and bitten; has different tastes; enters through the mouth. Energy: helps the body move; cannot be seen but can be felt; comes from nutrients. Food helps the body get energy.
